name: Devil’s Margarita
description: A tequila sour served up with a float of dry red wine, which sits on top like a layer of blood.
history: A modern bar riff that borrows the red wine float from the New York Sour and puts it on a margarita.
whyItWorks: Lime and tequila make a sharp sour; the dry red wine adds tannin and dark fruit and sits on top, so the first sips taste different from the last.

ingredients.label: Dry red wine, for the float

steps: Shake tequila, lime and simple syrup hard with ice.
Pour the red wine slowly over the back of a bar spoon so it floats on top.
techniqueNotes: A fruity, medium-bodied red (Malbec, Zinfandel, Syrah) floats and tastes better than a light one.
